page: Microsoft Azure F16amds_v7 is an AMD EPYC-based virtual machine categorized under the Compute Optimized server family with memory-intensive specifications. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via Microsoft Hyper-V, it provides 16 dedicated physical cores running 16 vCPUs at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz using AMD EPYC 9V45 processors. The instance includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside support for instruction sets including AVX-512 (F, VNNI, BF16), SHA-NI, and VAES. There are zero GPUs configured on this instance type.

Memory and storage allocations are balanced around high capacity. The instance provides 128.0 GB of system memory, representing an 8:1 ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is bundled via a local 1890 GB NVMe SSD drive capable of high-throughput local scratch or caching operations, alongside support for Azure Premium Storage. The server does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional single-thread capabilities. The single-core stress-ng metric reached 3354.98, placing it in the top 10%, complemented by strong bzip3 single-threaded decompression at 15.98 GB/sec and gzip compression at 36.17 GB/sec. Text generation on small 135M parameter LLM inference achieved top-tier performance at 420.78 tokens per second. Multi-core performance is solid, showing a stress-ng multi-core score of 53607.09 and a PassMark CPU score of 41088.1, both within the middle 50% distribution. Memory bandwidth registered at 108.05 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 68.96 GB/sec for writes.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high RAM-to-vCPU ratio combined with dedicated single-threaded cores and substantial onboard NVMe storage minimizes the need to over-provision compute cores solely to acquire memory or fast local storage. This profile serves memory-heavy compute tasks, medium-sized in-memory caches, database operations, and data transformation jobs that require both high per-thread performance and generous memory allocations.
description: Microsoft Azure F16amds_v7 is a compute-focused yet memory-dense virtual machine featuring 16 dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 cores (16 vCPUs) operating at up to 4.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM (8.0 GB per core) and bundled with a local 1890 GB NVMe SSD, it delivers high single-threaded performance alongside ample memory capacity. Benchmark data shows top-tier single-core CPU throughput (stress-ng score of 3354.98) and leading small-model LLM text generation rates, with mid-range multi-core compute and memory bandwidth figures. The instance lacks dedicated GPUs and complimentary public IPv4 addresses, focusing instead on solid sustained performance and low-latency local storage. It is well suited for memory-intensive compute jobs, local database operations, data transformation pipelines, and high-throughput caching environments.
